text: Most adults should aim for roughly 45-65% of daily calories from carbohydrates, 20-35% from fat, and 10-35% from protein, built around vegetables, fruit, whole grains, lean protein and dairy or alternatives. (baseline macro split percentage carbs fat protein limits distributions options dietary values)

Added sugars should stay under 10% of daily calories and saturated fat under 10% of daily calories, with most fat coming from unsaturated sources like oils, nuts and fish. (daily limit added sugar saturated fat restriction health guidelines percentage maximum thresholds)

Adults are advised to keep sodium intake under 2,300mg a day, mainly by limiting processed and packaged foods rather than table salt alone. (recommended sodium limit salt intake per day restriction mg levels consumer guidelines)

Adults should get at least 150-300 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity, or 75-150 minutes of vigorous activity, per week, spread across most days. (cardio weekly aerobic exercise target minutes physical target framework health goals)

Muscle-strengthening activity that works all major muscle groups is recommended on 2 or more days per week, in addition to aerobic activity. (strength training often how many days beginner lift weights weekly recommendations exercise gym routines)

Some activity is better than none, and benefits start accumulating from the very first minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity, even below the full weekly target. (rest days train same muscles row recovery benefit light physical work)

For workouts longer than about an hour, a carbohydrate-containing snack 30-60 minutes beforehand helps sustain energy, and easily digestible carbs during very long sessions can help maintain performance. (pre workout meal eat before training energy fueling long active routines)

Rather than one large protein-heavy meal, spreading protein across meals and snacks throughout the day supports muscle repair after training. (spread protein across meals spread out intake several small ones amino distribution balance strategy)

Drinking water before, during and after exercise helps prevent dehydration; pale yellow urine is a simple everyday indicator of adequate hydration. (water drink during exercise workout hydration electrolytes long training fluid balance indicators)

A simple way to build a meal is to fill half the plate with vegetables and fruit, a quarter with lean protein, and a quarter with whole grains or starchy vegetables. (plate look like balanced meal plate layout structure portion control sizes building options)

Cutting back on highly processed, energy-dense snacks and sugary drinks is one of the most effective ways to reduce excess calorie intake without tracking every gram. (plate look like balanced meal plate options snacks calories tracking management guidelines)

A full meal 3-4 hours before training allows time for digestion, while a smaller carbohydrate-focused snack 30-60 minutes before can top up energy without causing stomach discomfort. (pre workout meal eat before training timing hours preworkout digestion comfort windows)

Consuming carbohydrate and protein within about 2 hours after training supports glycogen replenishment and muscle repair; the exact minute-by-minute window is less critical than getting this in during the day. (eat after workout recover training post snack recovery window timeline eating sports nutrition)

For sessions over 60-90 minutes or heavy sweating, replacing sodium and other electrolytes alongside fluids helps maintain performance and prevent cramping. (water drink during exercise workout electrolytes long training sessions sweat performance recovery fluids)

Batch-preparing simple meals built around a protein source, a carbohydrate source and vegetables makes it easier to eat consistently around a training schedule. (set up basic meal prep batch prepare consistent training systems structural cooking ideas)

Convenient post-training snacks that pair carbs and protein include a yoghurt with fruit, a glass of milk, or a sandwich with lean protein filling. (eat after workout recover training post snack good options macro snack combinations sports menu)

For people doing regular resistance training, roughly 1.6g of protein per kilogram of bodyweight per day maximises muscle protein synthesis, with little extra benefit found above about 2.2g/kg/day. (protein need muscle gain ideal daily lifting weights total mass requirement parameters optimization)

Distributing protein into 3-4 meals of roughly 0.4g per kilogram of bodyweight each appears more effective for muscle growth than concentrating it into one or two large meals. (protein need muscle gain spread out meals several small ones growth macro distribution strategy optimization)

Hitting total daily protein intake is a stronger driver of muscle growth than the exact timing of protein relative to a workout, though eating protein within a few hours of training is still a reasonable habit. (protein need muscle gain ideal daily lifting weights timing windows routine behavior)

New members are typically advised to start with 2-3 full-body strength sessions a week, focusing on major compound movements, before progressing to more specialised splits. (strength training often how many days beginner lift weights gym sessions onboarding schedules)

For general strength and muscle goals, resting 60-90 seconds between sets is a common starting point, with longer rests (2-3 minutes) for heavier, lower-rep lifting. (long should rest between sets recovery intervals breathing break protocols)

New members can book a free induction session with a trainer to learn correct form on the main equipment before training independently. (gym induction book session trainer formal instruction orientation onboarding class help)

WHO recommends adults do at least 150-300 minutes of moderate-intensity or 75-150 minutes of vigorous-intensity aerobic activity weekly, plus muscle-strengthening activity on 2+ days. (cardio weekly aerobic exercise target minutes duration instructions options guidelines)

Limiting long periods of sitting and replacing sedentary time with activity of any intensity is associated with health benefits, independent of meeting the weekly activity target. (sedentary sitting behaviors active displacement lifestyle rules guidelines standard)

Older adults, pregnant and postpartum people, and those with chronic conditions can generally follow the same broad activity targets, adapted in intensity, with balance-focused activity recommended for older adults. (exercise advice different older adults pregnant members modified routines guidelines considerations)

Muscle-strengthening activities include lifting weights, working with resistance bands, bodyweight exercises like push-ups and squats, and heavy gardening or carrying loads. (exercises count muscle strengthening activity lifting tracking types baseline modalities)

Stretching and balance exercises, such as yoga or tai chi, are encouraged alongside strength and aerobic work, particularly for older adults to help reduce fall risk. (stretching balance work flexibility routine safety training fall prevention guidelines options)

Allowing at least one rest or light-activity day between intense strength sessions targeting the same muscle groups helps the body recover and adapt. (rest days train same muscles row recovery window physical tissue repair rules system)

For optimal health and cardiorespiratory conditioning, adults may substitute or combine traditional aerobic blocks with high-intensity interval training (HIIT) sessions, which evoke similar metabolic adaptations in less time. (hiit instead of normal steady state cardio exercise alternative high intensity intervals)

Healthy older adults should incorporate multicomponent physical activity that emphasizes functional balance and strength training at moderate or greater intensity on 3 or more days per week to enhance functional capacity and prevent falls. (seniors elders aging recommendations training guidelines older adults fall protection stability physical targets)

During pregnancy and the postpartum period, individuals without medical contraindications should achieve at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic physical activity weekly, incorporating gentle muscle-strengthening work. (pregnant woman women guidelines advice safety prenatal postpartum metrics training targets)

To mitigate the structural degradation of cartilage, dynamic weight-bearing exercise is recommended, as regular mechanical loading promotes joint lubrication and chondrocyte health without accelerating osteoarthritis. (clicking popping cracking joints health protection skeletal movement systems density dynamic loading)

Static stretching should ideally be performed when muscles are thoroughly warmed up after training rather than before, holding each major muscle group elongation for 10 to 30 seconds to safely improve range of motion. (stretch safely flexibility routine duration workout static holds lengthening mobility blocks)

An ultra-processed food diet rich in refined emulsifiers and artificial flavorings modifies the gut microbiome and triggers systematic low-grade inflammation, making an avoidance of these foods central to metabolic health. (junk food bad nutrition dangers inflammatory items digestion changes microflora criteria)

Inadequate sleep (under 7 hours per night) fundamentally impairs athletic recovery by suppressing human growth hormone (HGH) secretion, disrupting insulin sensitivity, and escalating performance-limiting cortisol production. (lack of sleep rest impact muscle growth hormones tired overnight recovery sleep architecture patterns)

To prevent acute hyponatremia during prolonged endurance training over 90 minutes, fluid consumption should closely match individual sweat rates rather than excessively exceeding them with plain water alone. (avoid overhydrating dehydration water intoxication cramping minerals fluid calculations endurance safe levels)

Consuming 3-5mg of caffeine per kilogram of body weight roughly 30-60 minutes before training significantly reduces the rate of perceived exertion (RPE) and increases total power output during resistance tasks. (pre workout stimulant dosage energy benefits strength caffeine intake stimulant timing targets efficiency)

Creatine monohydrate supplementation at a stable daily dose of 3-5 grams safely increases intramuscular phosphocreatine stores, directly accelerating ATP resynthesis during short, explosive bursts of heavy lifting. (explosive strength building safe effective supplements creatine monohydrate cellular energy power loading rules)

Consuming high-quality dairy proteins containing native whey and micellar casein before sleep provides a sustained release of amino acids throughout the night, supporting skeletal muscle protein synthesis during overnight fasts. (casein protein shake before bed shake benefits recovery nighttime feeding strategy amino distribution fasts)
